This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.

Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.
Track experiments and model versions and support monitoring and CI/CD processes.
Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.
Learn codebase, development workflows, and platform fundamentals through pairing and code reviews.

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or relevant STEM certification; or 4 years of equivalent experience.

Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases

CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

AbbVie’s Global Forecasting Center of Excellence (COE) sustains and advances the organization’s volume forecasting capabilities established under Finance Transformation Forecasting Excellence. The COE defines forecasting standards, governs best practices, oversees deployment of enabling technologies, executes centralized forecasting functions on behalf of the organization, and builds forecasting competencies across AbbVie’s US, International, and Allergan Aesthetics commercial organizations.
The COE’s Operations & Insights pillar is the operational and analytical engine that powers enterprise forecasting at scale, encompassing AI and statistical modeling and governance, forecasting platform management, and centralized analytics. The Enterprise Forecasting Platform team is a key component of the COE and is responsible for the business ownership, operation, adoption, and continued evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform.
Position Overview
The Associate Director, Enterprise Forecasting Platform Product Owner is accountable for the business ownership, strategy, ongoing management, and evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform. The role owns the product vision and roadmap, prioritizes capabilities and enhancements, drives adoption and effective utilization, oversees platform economics, and ensures the product continues to meet evolving enterprise forecasting needs.
This role serves as a key business owner of the relationship with the platform vendor. It establishes platform performance expectations, manages service levels and commitments, oversees adoption and utilization measures, and ensures AbbVie realizes appropriate value from its investment.
The Product Owner works closely with forecasters, Finance leadership, Forecasting COE teams, Business Technology Solutions (BTS), data and analytics partners, Procurement, and the platform vendor to translate business needs into platform priorities and deliver an effective foundation for enterprise forecasting processes.
Core Job Responsibilities:
Enterprise Product Ownership & Strategy
Serve as the business product owner for AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform, accountable for overall business value, usability, adoption, and continued evolution.
Define and maintain the product vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Global Forecasting COE priorities and enterprise business needs.
Develop and manage strategic and tactical roadmaps that translate forecasting needs into sequenced platform capabilities and enhancements.
Own business prioritization of platform features, functionality, integrations, and enhancements.
Maintain and prioritize the business product backlog in partnership with BTS, the vendor, the COE, Finance, and forecasting stakeholders.
Establish clear prioritization criteria based on enterprise value, user impact, cost, risk, implementation complexity, and operational readiness.
Evaluate opportunities to expand or improve platform capabilities as forecasting processes, analytical methods, data availability, and technologies evolve.
Vendor & Commercial Management
Own the strategic business relationship with the enterprise forecasting platform vendor and serve as the primary point of accountability for vendor performance.
Define, monitor, and enforce vendor success measures and service-level agreements (SLAs).
Establish regular vendor governance and performance reporting covering enhancements, defects, service levels, contractual commitments, open issues, risks, and remediation plans.
Hold the vendor accountable for delivery against agreed priorities, timelines, service expectations, and contractual obligations.
Partner with Procurement, BTS, Finance, Legal, and other functions on contract renewals, commercial discussions, and vendor evaluations.
Monitor platform consumption and contractual usage where applicable and identify potential cost, capacity, or service implications.
Maintain visibility into total product cost and value, including vendor fees and associated investments required to operate and enhance the platform.
Assess whether the vendor roadmap and capabilities remain aligned with AbbVie’s evolving forecasting needs.
Platform Implementation, Operations & Continuous Improvement
Oversee the business implementation of platform releases, enhancements, and new capabilities, ensuring solutions meet agreed requirements and compliance expectations.
Partner with BTS and the vendor to translate forecasting needs into clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation priorities.
Establish processes for intake, triage, prioritization, escalation, and resolution of platform issues and enhancement requests.
Monitor platform performance and user experience, identifying recurring friction points and opportunities to simplify or improve forecasting workflows.
Ensure platform changes consider impacts to upstream data, forecasting processes, analytical outputs, downstream planning activities, and end users.
Maintain product documentation, decision history, requirements, roadmap materials, operational procedures, and key institutional knowledge.
Drive continuous product improvement.
Adoption & Capability Building
Partner with COE and the Forecast Excellence team to champion the forecasting platform across the organization, create a clear understanding of its value and appropriate use, and identify and address barriers to adoption.
Develop a structured approach for measuring platform adoption, utilization, user experience, and business value.
Build feedback mechanisms that allow forecasters and Finance stakeholders to influence product priorities while maintaining disciplined enterprise governance.
Translate platform capabilities into clear, practical implications for forecasting teams.
Stakeholder Management & Governance
Act as the primary business interface among forecasting users, COE leadership, Finance leadership, BTS, data and analytics teams, Procurement, and the platform vendor.
Capture and synthesize requirements from brands, geographies, and forecasting teams into enterprise-level priorities.
Proactively manage expectations regarding roadmap priorities, delivery timing, platform limitations, dependencies, and tradeoffs.
Establish transparent governance for major product decisions and investment priorities.
Regularly communicate the product roadmap, progress, risks, adoption, issues, vendor performance, and business value to COE and Finance leadership.
Co-Lead workshops and decision forums (in partnership with Standards and Training) needed to align stakeholders around product choices and future capabilities.
Escalate material platform or vendor risks and drive them through resolution.
Financial & Resource Management
Develop and manage the business case and budget associated with the enterprise forecasting platform.
Maintain transparency into platform costs, vendor spend, enhancement investments, and required resources.
Evaluate the costs, expected benefits, and organizational implications of significant platform enhancements and investments.
Partner with Finance, BTS, Procurement, and COE leadership to inform investment and resource-allocation decisions.
Identify opportunities to improve the economic efficiency of the platform while protecting critical enterprise forecasting capabilities.
Team / People Leadership
Lead and guide team members supporting forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support as the operating model evolves.
Own prioritization and work planning for the team, ensuring resources are allocated to the highest-value platform needs.
Provide regular feedback, coaching, and career-development support to team members.
Build strong product-management capability within the Operations & Insights organization.
Create a culture of user orientation, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Reporting
Reports to: Director, Forecasting Operations & Insights
Direct reports: Team members supporting enterprise forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support, with size determined by the evolving operating model.
ualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Analytics, Information Technology, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in product management, platform ownership, forecasting, analytics, technology-enabled business transformation, or related roles.
Demonstrated experience owning or managing a complex enterprise technology product or platform through implementation, adoption, optimization, and ongoing evolution.
Demonstrated ability to develop product strategies and roadmaps and translate business needs into prioritized technology capabilities and requirements.
Experience managing external technology or platform vendors, including performance, delivery commitments, issue escalation, and commercial considerations.
Strong understanding of enterprise data, analytics, technology, and the dependencies required to operationalize technology-enabled business processes.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with business, data, analytics, and technology teams and translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to lead complex, matrixed initiatives involving multiple stakeholder groups and competing priorities.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder-management skills, including experience communicating product decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders.
Ability to operate effectively under ambiguity, make disciplined prioritization decisions, and manage multiple concurrent priorities.
Preferred:
Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, life sciences, or another complex global commercial organization.
Experience with commercial forecasting, financial planning, analytics, or decision-support platforms.
Familiarity with pharmaceutical volume forecasting and planning cycles such as LBE, Plan, and LRP.
Experience managing enterprise software-as-a-service platforms and vendor relationships.
Experience establishing product governance, adoption metrics, service expectations, and product-performance reporting.
Experience working with forecasting or planning technologies and their supporting data ecosystems.

Acting effectively as a principal investigator, the candidate will generate original technical ideas and development strategies, serve as the accountable engineering leader for complex multidisciplinary challenges, and make timely, well-reasoned recommendations when the evidence base is incomplete – clearly communicating assumptions, trade-offs, risks, and mitigations. Lead the Cross-Functional Modeling Forum (CMF): set the agenda, convene modeling practitioners from R&D, Operations, and partner functions, and establish the governance, review cycles, decision rights, and model credibility standards that keep the organization’s computational practices effective, current, and aligned with business strategy.
Lead the Computational Assisted Process Engineering (CAPE) group: directly supervise, mentor, and develop a team of modeling engineers; evaluate individual performance and own accountability for the effective performance of the team; sponsor emerging leaders, design meaningful development assignments, and recommend resource allocations.
Coordinate AI activities across the entire Small Molecule (SM) CMC organization: drive best-practice sharing and AI tool management, and guide, train, and motivate colleagues in the effective use of AI.
Set and communicate the computational process engineering strategy across drug-development programs and major capabilities, aligning technical priorities, resource recommendations, and risk decisions with program and portfolio needs.
Own the integrated computational engineering strategy from laboratory and modeling understanding through scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing readiness; define critical uncertainties, scale-up strategy, and manufacturing-readiness criteria, and direct the generation of data required to test key hypotheses.
Function as a principal investigator: independently conceive, execute, and communicate novel multi-disciplinary modeling and development strategies that achieve project and area goals, while contributing scientific insight to multiple other projects.
Direct the development, qualification, and deployment of multi-physics and mechanistic models – including CFD, discrete element and particle-based methods, structural, thermal, and fluid-structure interaction analysis, transport phenomena, reaction and crystallization kinetics, and reduced-order or hybrid digital twins – to address equipment design, process design space definition, scale-up, and manufacturing challenges.
Anticipate future program and portfolio challenges and establish new engineering strategies, technical proposals, and capability investments that address emerging scientific, regulatory, and manufacturing needs; recommend build, buy, partner, or stop decisions for modeling tools, platforms, and workstreams.
Serve as the accountable engineering leader for complex, multidisciplinary technical issues; establish decision criteria, lead the resolution of unprecedented problems, and provide decisive consultation to multiple programs and partner functions.
Champion creative, ‘out of the box’ thinking and new technologies – including advanced simulation methods, automation, surrogate and machine-learning-assisted modeling, high-performance and cloud computing, and modern data and software engineering practices – and move them from demonstration into routine, governed program use.

Champion a safe, compliant, inclusive, and high-learning culture; set clear expectations, reinforce constructive challenge, and convert lessons learned from programs, campaigns, and audits into sustainable systems and practices.
Shape Process Engineering and Center of Excellence strategy through long-range capability planning, talent priorities, resource recommendations, and cross-functional operating models.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, GxP compliance, and animal care where applicable.
Qualifications:
PhD with 5+ years of experience in area or scientific area of discipline. Demonstrated depth in computational engineering, with several years of applied, industrially relevant experience in multi-physics simulation and a proven record of translating simulation results into design, process, or manufacturing decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading a small team of engineers with strong modeling competence, including delegation of meaningful ownership, technical coaching, performance feedback, and accountability for team deliverables.
Proven command of engineering fundamentals – fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, solid mechanics, thermodynamics, mixing, and reaction engineering – combined with the numerical methods, meshing, solver, and convergence judgment required to produce trustworthy results.
Proficiency with leading commercial and open-source simulation environments (e.g., ANSYS Fluent or Mechanical, COMSOL Multiphysics, STAR-CCM+, Abaqus, OpenFOAM) and with scientific programming and data workflows in Python, MATLAB, or an equivalent ecosystem.
Demonstrated ability to solve difficult technical problems, champion new technologies, and establish new capabilities that achieve project and organizational goals.
Demonstrated scientific and organizational leadership, with the influence and credibility to lead a cross-functional forum, align stakeholders with competing priorities, and drive consensus on methods, standards, and investment.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex computational concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for technical experts, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another regulated industry, including exposure to GxP compliance, technology transfer, and CMC regulatory content.
Experience applying computational methods to pharmaceutical unit operations such as mixing and blending, crystallization, filtration and drying, lyophilization, granulation, tableting, spray drying, sterile and aseptic processing, single-use systems, or fill-finish.
Experience with discrete element modeling (DEM), population balance modeling, multiphase and free-surface flows, non-Newtonian rheology, and coupled CFD-DEM or fluid-structure interaction approaches.
Experience with mechanistic process modeling, flowsheet simulation, digital twins, and model-based design space definition in support of Quality by Design.

location: Cambridge, MA, US
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team is focused on identifying new targets for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases through computational analysis of human disease tissue-derived datasets and validating targets using humanized experimental approaches.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. If you are passionate about translating complex biological data into actionable insights and advancing personalized medicine, we encourage you to apply.
This position will be based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and requires passion, attention to detail, prior hands-on experience, and teamwork.
Key Responsibilities:
Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.

title: Policy Lead, California
location: California, United States
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's US & Canada Public Policy team represents Airbnb and the interests of our community of hosts and guests before the legislators, regulators, opinion leaders and coalitions who shape the political and legal environment for our business. We operate in heavily regulated spaces in the technology sector: short-term rental rules are written and rewritten at the state, county and municipal level, and the outcomes directly determine where and how Airbnb can grow.
The Difference You Will Make:
The Policy Lead, California holds ultimate responsibility for Airbnb's public policy and regulatory strategy in the state. This is a senior leadership position accountable for three interlocking outcomes:
Business growth. Protecting and expanding Airbnb's ability to operate across California by securing workable regulatory frameworks at the state and local level and defending against measures that would restrict supply or impose restrictive compliance burdens.
Regulatory affairs. Managing an active, high-volume docket of state legislation, local ordinances, administrative rulemaking and enforcement,  ensuring Airbnb's position is well represented in each.
Brand reputation among policymakers. Above all, materially improving how lawmakers, regulators and civic leaders perceive Airbnb and its host community, and converting that credibility into durable policy outcomes.
The role is as much internal as it is external. You will  lead a team of Policy Managers covering California's priority markets, manage a bench of external consultants and lobbyists, and be accountable for the state's annual policy budget. Equally important, the Lead serves as the central point of alignment between Public Policy and the cross-functional partners whose decisions shape our regulatory position: Legal, Supply, Communications, Marketing, Safety, Tax, and the business leadership for the region. Success requires building consensus across these functions on a single integrated strategy and then driving its execution.
The Policy Lead reports to the US and Canada Policy Strategy Director and works in close collaboration with the Head of Public Policy and the broader policy leadership team.
A Typical Day:
Set and own the California strategy:
Develop and own a fully integrated, multi-year state and local public policy strategy for California, grounded in data, political analysis and a clear-eyed assessment of regulatory risk and growth opportunity.
Prioritize across a large and dynamic portfolio of state bills, local ordinances, ballot measures, administrative proceedings, allocating team, consultant and financial resources to the matters that most affect the business.
Define measurable objectives for the state and report progress, risks and outcomes to the Director and senior business leadership on a regular cadence.
Own and manage the California policy budget, including consultant and lobbyist engagements, campaign tactics such as paid media, research, programs and political engagement, ensuring resources are deployed against strategic priorities.
Lead cross-functional alignment:
Serve as Public Policy's primary counterpart to Legal on California matters, partnering on strategy, regulatory interpretation and compliance.
Work with Supply leadership to align regulatory strategy with growth targets, understand the on-the-ground impact of proposed rules, and shape product and operational responses to regulation.
Partner with Communications and Marketing to build and execute reputation strategies directed at policymakers and the civic audiences who influence them, including narrative development, earned and paid media, research publication and third-party validation.
Ensure that internal stakeholders at every level understand the California strategy, that information flows to those who need it, and that roadblocks and wins are surfaced early.
Drive external advocacy and reputation:
Represent Airbnb at the most senior levels of California state and local government, including legislative leadership, the Governor's office, state agencies, mayors, county supervisors and city councils.
Build and sustain a broad network of relationships across legislative, executive and administrative offices, and with the coalitions, trade associations, labor, housing and tourism stakeholders whose positions shape outcomes.
Deploy the full range of advocacy tools available to a regulated marketplace: direct lobbying, coalition campaigns, host and guest mobilization, economic impact research, paid and earned media, political strategy.
Serve as a spokesperson on California policy matters as needed, in coordination with Communications.
Negotiate directly with government counterparts to secure regulatory frameworks that are workable for hosts and consistent with Airbnb's national and global approach.
Build and lead the team:
Lead, coach and develop a team of Policy Managers and the consultants who support them, setting clear objectives, holding the team accountable for results, and investing in their growth as strategists and advocates.
Own recruitment, performance management and succession planning for the California team.
Foster an inclusive, high-performing culture consistent with Airbnb's core values, and create opportunities for team members to lead projects that stretch their strategic and operational skills.
Ensure consultants and lobbyists are properly briefed, aligned to strategy and delivering measurable value.
Your Expertise:
12 to 15+ years of progressively senior experience in public policy, government relations, political campaigns, public affairs or regulatory strategy, in a corporate, consulting, governmental or advocacy setting.
Deep knowledge of California politics and government, including the Legislature, state agencies and major local jurisdictions, and an established network of relationships across them.
Demonstrated success leading strategy in a heavily regulated or politically contested industry; experience in travel, housing, technology platforms or other regulated marketplaces is strongly preferred.
Proven track record of changing how policymakers perceive an organization or issue, and of translating improved reputation into concrete legislative or regulatory outcomes.
Experience leading integrated advocacy campaigns that combine direct lobbying with coalition building, grassroots mobilization, research and paid and earned media.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional alignment at senior levels, build consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, and drive a shared strategy to execution.
Senior people-leadership experience, including hiring, performance management, coaching and developing a multidisciplinary team; experience managing external consultants and lobbyists.
Strong command of budget planning and resource allocation in a results-driven environment.
Ability to rapidly absorb complex legislative, regulatory and technical material and translate it into clear positions and compelling advocacy.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the credibility to represent Airbnb before senior government officials, the media and internal executives.
Experience on political campaigns, in public relations or public affairs, or in strategic consulting is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in law, public policy or a related field preferred.

title: Program Manager, Global Retail Demo Operations, Retail Experience
location: Seattle, Washington, USA
description:
The Program Manager, Global Retail Demo Operations owns the end-to-end lifecycle of the demo devices that bring Amazon Devices to life in physical retail: Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, Alexa Tablet, Ring, and Blink. From the first demand signal at NPI through factory demo conversion, delivery to fixture vendors and stores, and sustaining replacement, this role makes sure the right device, in the right configuration, with the right content, lands in the right place on time, in every region where we sell.
This is a builder role. Today much of demo planning runs on spreadsheets, email threads, and individual follow-up. You will replace that with scalable mechanisms: a single global intake and ordering system, factory-level conversion at scale, documented approval gates, and dashboards that let stakeholders see status without asking. You will look across North America, Europe, Japan, Australia, and emerging markets and find where we can standardize, automate, and remove cost.
Based in Seattle, you are the single point of contact for demo orders from Channel Marketing teams worldwide, and you partner withNPI program and operations teams, Demand Planning, Trade Compliance, Legal/Contracts, Demo Software and Content teams, factories, and a global network of fixture vendors. You will own outcomes that are measured in launch readiness, order accuracy, and cost per unit.
Key job responsibilities
Global Demo Order Management
Own the global demo order process. Channel Marketing teammates in every region (North America, Europe, Japan, and other markets) submit their demo needs to you, and you run those orders from intake to delivery. Set the intake standard and calendar, validate each request against the fixture footprint, repair-and-maintenance buffers, and push back when quantities, timing, or configurations don't add up. Run the confidence progression (low → medium → high) against each program's NPI schedule, lock ASIN-level demand (demo SKU vs. fresh lot), and place final orders with the factory. Keep every Channel Marketer informed through one source of truth showing each order's status, ship date, tracking, and destination, so they never have to chase it.
Factory Demo Conversions
Lead the shift from vendor-performed demo conversion to factory conversion, a step change in cost per unit and speed to shelf. Define conversion specs per device, retailer, and region (content package, network profile, retail configuration). Bring North America to factory conversion for new launches, then extend the model to every region, with a clear migration plan for fixture vendors and stakeholders.
Launch Readiness & NPI Demo Last Mile
Run the weekly Demo Launch Readiness rhythm across product lines: demo experience readiness, content status, software flags, factory build and conversion status, and arrival at fixture vendors. Tie every program's announce date, street date, vendor disclosure window, and fixture in-store date into one plan, and call out risks early enough to change the outcome.
Demo Content, Configuration & Approval Gates
Own the gate before any mass conversion or deployment. Validate that demo content is live and correct in the right demo administration orgs, generate device-specific demo builds with the software team, and maintain default demo configurations for new launches. Run a documented first-article approval (proof of conversion → sign-off → release to mass production) with a full audit trail by device, retailer, region, and content version.
Vendor NDAs, MEAs, Disclosure & Chain of Custody
Own the vendor NDA and material evaluation agreement (MEA) process end to end. Request and route agreements through Contracts and Security approvals, keep a live record of which fixture and display vendors are approved for which programs and what they may receive (pre-release devices, CAD files, product information), and enforce the timing rules that govern vendor disclosure ahead of announce. Onboard new vendors and new product lines as they come up. Track pre-release hardware by device serial number with full chain of custody, and partner with Trade Compliance on cross-border movement and customs.
Prototype, Non-Powered & Packaging Units
Signal prototype availability at each hardware cycle (EVT/DVT/PVT), own allocation and budget, and prevent shortages that block fixture development. Extend the same ordering mechanism to non-powered demo shells, dummy units, and empty retail packaging for displays
Third-Party Demo Components
Own demo power supplies, cables, and other components not supplied by the factory. Manage suppliers, long lead times, and inventory positioning so components arrive with the devices, in every region.
Global Mechanisms, Automation & Data
Design and ship the systems that make this role scale: a structured global intake with auto-populated device data and suggested quantities, automated status reporting, and integrations with roadmap, catalog/ASIN, fixture, and project-management systems. Use automation and AI tools to remove manual steps. Write the SOPs so the work does not depend on any one person, then roll them out region by region.
A day in the life
How They Deliver
• Stakeholders can check order, conversion, and shipment status themselves, without asking.
• Channel Marketing teams in every region submit demo orders through one process and get them on time, in the right quantity and configuration.
• Devices arrive at the correct vendor or store, in the correct quantity and configuration, ahead of fixture build and install dates.
• Cost per converted unit drops as conversions move to the factory, region by region.
• Every pre-release device is tracked by serial number with documented chain of custody.
• Every vendor has the NDA and MEA it needs before it receives devices or information, with no launch delayed by a missing agreement.
• No program is blocked by a prototype, component, or disclosure gap that could have been forecast.
• Weekly Demo Launch Readiness runs on time, on agenda, with clear owners and decisions.
• Write narratives, SOPs, and business reviews (MBR/QBR, PR/FAQ) that drive decisions and earn trust across teams and regions.
• Identify the next mechanism to build or automate, and land it, without being asked.
• Mentor partners and peers on demo planning, and contribute to a culture of documentation and continuous improvement.
Basic qualifications: - 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Preferred qualifications: - 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- 3+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

title: Sr Product Manager, OTS Delivery Software Engineering (DSE)
location: Austin, Texas, USA
description:
Every Amazon package that ships, every grocery order that is fulfilled, and every associate who needs IT help depends on technology our teams keep running. Amazon's OpsTech Solutions (OTS) is the IT operations and infrastructure organization for all of Amazon Worldwide Operations, including Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), delivering reliable technology to more than one million associates and operators across every geography. OTS is transforming from reactive support to proactive, prescriptive, AI-powered service delivery, and ServiceNow is the platform where that work happens.
What this role is: You will own the product experience for how work moves between ServiceNow and other ticketing platforms (e.g. SIM-T) and the integration strategy that lets OTS scale as more partner teams and platforms connect. Cross-organization resolver groups depend on SIM-T, so the connection to ServiceNow has to work reliably. Better integration gives our customers the information they need when they need it, wherever they are. You will decide what information synchronizes, how paging and engagement work, and how the integration grows as new partner teams are added.
Our team is organized around three questions that apply to every persona we serve: How does someone ask for help? How does the organization receive and organize that work? How does the work get resolved? This role sits where the answers meet other organizations. OTS depends on these integrations to send work items to teams outside the OTS organization. Your peers own the requester front door (OneSupportHub and Virtual Agent), the Incident Management Platform (ITSM), Service Desk Workforce Optimization, and AI resolution intelligence (OTS Assist and PathFinder). The decisions you make determine whether work reaches the right team with the right context, and whether those peers' products work as intended once work leaves ServiceNow.
The opportunity is to turn a fragile integration into a well-governed product. You will define the fields and information that synchronize between platforms, the paging and engagement models, the experience for managing CTI to category/subcategory mapping, and the governance for how catalog item flows synchronize. You will also define the integration strategy as the business scales. As more partner teams and platforms need to send work to OTS or receive work from it, you will set the principles, standards, and requirements for how those integrations are built, onboarded, and governed, and you will keep OTS's needs represented as that work evolves. The SIM-T work gives you a strong foundation, because the lessons from that integration become the pattern for every new connection. Your customers are Service Desk fulfillers, Field IT technicians and managers, and the partner teams that send and receive OTS work.
Key Highlights
• Own the product experience for ServiceNow integration, from paging and escalation to information synchronization.
• Define the data, paging, and engagement models that govern work sent to teams outside OTS.
• Own the experience for CTI to category/subcategory mapping and the governance of catalog item flow synchronization.
• Define the integration strategy that lets OTS scale as the business grows, and partner with external teams.
• Work at the center of a product team whose adjacent products (intake, ITSM, routing, workforce optimization, AI resolution) all depend on work moving reliably between systems.
Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the product vision and roadmap for ServiceNow integration with SIM-T and other ticketing platforms, and prioritize improvements against the gaps customers experience.
- Define which fields and lifecycle events synchronize between platforms, including status, severity, type conversion, transfers, and escalation, and the rules for resolving conflicts.
- Design paging and engagement models so partner teams are contacted correctly and do not receive duplicate or misrouted pages.
- Define the UI/UX for managing CTI to category/subcategory mapping, working with UX and engineering partners.
- Establish governance for catalog item flow synchronization, including how new catalog items and partner teams are onboarded.
- Act as the voice of the customer for Service Desk, Field IT, and partner teams, using shadowing, feedback, and operational data to translate real workflow friction into prioritized requirements.
- Define and maintain OTS's integration strategy and standards for partner platforms and teams, including what data and context pass between systems and how new integrations are onboarded, in partnership with partner teams.
- Set up an intake and prioritization process for new integration requests, so OTS can decide consistently what to accept, defer, or decline.
- Contribute to annual planning mechanisms (OP1/OP2) with clear, well-reasoned investment proposals, and maintain mechanisms to continuously capture voice of the customer.
A day in the life
Your day moves between the floor and the roadmap. You might start by reviewing a handful of tickets that failed to sync, tracing where information was lost and which rule needs to change. Midday, you meet with a partner platform team to decide which integration requirements are in scope for the next phase and how they fit the broader integration strategy. In the afternoon, you work with UX and engineering on a mapping workflow for CTI to category/subcategory, meet with a partner team that wants to start sending work to OTS, and draft a requirements document or an OP2 investment proposal for senior review.

The ServiceNow Product Management team builds the products that are the backbone of OTS operations. Amazon employees, Service Desk agents, and Field IT technicians rely on these ServiceNow experiences to complete their work every day. The team is a group of Product Managers, each owning one clear product space so they can go deep instead of switching between unrelated problems, supported by a dedicated UX designer. Your engineering counterparts sit within the same larger organization, and your primary stakeholders are the Service Desk and Field IT organizations and the partner teams outside OTS that send and receive work.

title: Sr. Regulatory Technical program Manager, Direct-to-Device (D2D), Amazon Leo, Regulatory, Authorization Readiness & Compliance (ARC)
location: Arlington, Virginia, USA
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's initiative to launch a constellation of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to provide affordable, reliable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Direct-to-Device (D2D) is a groundbreaking service that will bring satellite connectivity directly to everyday mobile devices, extending coverage beyond the reach of traditional terrestrial networks. To enable this, the Regulatory team obtains licenses and approvals for space, services, ground-based infrastructure, and the spectrum required to serve customers in each country where Amazon Leo will operate. There is no globally unified regulatory licensing regime for a LEO system like Amazon Leo, and most countries lack established D2D licensing frameworks entirely.
We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to join the Authorization Readiness and Compliance (ARC) team, a sub-function within the Regulatory organization at Amazon Leo. You will own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading implementation of the D2D-specific authorization plans defined by Regulatory Licensing Leads across priority countries. You will work directly with regional Regulatory TPMs, Legal, and Regulatory Licensing Leads to drive execution across FCC, ITU, and country regulators in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions, ensuring Amazon Leo can offer commercial D2D service on day one in every priority country.
D2D is a first-of-its-kind satellite service category. ITU rules continue to evolve, and jurisdictions impose conflicting spectrum and interference requirements. You will navigate that uncertainty, exercising independent judgment to implement the authorization readiness path forward where no clear precedent exists. This role demands technical fluency in Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum allocations, interference analysis, satellite communications, and 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards. You will lead the implementation of complex license conditions and, in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, translate obligations into precise engineering requirements that software and operations teams can act on. You will also design and build a licensing obligation tracking platform and automated compliance reporting pipeline to manage thousands of license conditions at scale.
Key job responsibilities
•Own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading the implementation of the authorization path, tracking milestones, and driving resolution of blockers across priority countries.
•Interpret complex license conditions across FCC, ITU, and country-level regulators, and in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, convert obligations into actionable engineering requirements for software and operations teams.
•Drive cross-functional coordination with engineering, infrastructure, business, and operations teams to align authorization timelines with service launch schedules.
•Influence without authority across senior stakeholders in matrixed organizations, resolving competing priorities between customer commitments, engineering constraints, and regulatory realities.
•Identify and escalate regulatory risks with clear mitigation strategies to maintain compliance and prevent operational disruptions.
•Provide senior leadership visibility on D2D authorization readiness, launch risk, and country-by-country compliance status.
•Own the regulatory stakeholder relationship with key customers and partners, delivering precise updates on D2D authorization status and maintaining trust through consistent follow-through.
•Set a course in the face of ambiguity to deliver independently, asking the right questions, clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately.
Export Control
This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.
A day in the life
You will serve as the critical link between the Regulatory team and the broader Amazon Leo organization, driving cross-functional priorities with engineering, infrastructure, and business teams, and providing senior leadership visibility into D2D authorization readiness and launch risk. A key part of this role is managing the regulatory relationship with customer and partner stakeholders who maintain high expectations for communication precision, timeline accuracy, and compliance rigor. You will translate complex, evolving regulatory positions into clear narratives, set and manage expectations across competing priorities, and maintain trust through disciplined follow-through. The right candidate will have successfully managed multi-discipline telecommunications program initiatives, possess a well-rounded technical background in satellite communications, and demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills.
About the team
The Regulatory team secures and safeguards Amazon Leo's access to radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbital resources around the world, addresses ground infrastructure licensing and regulatory requirements, and shapes the policies and regulatory requirements that affect our ability to deliver on business goals, enabling delivery of broadband and D2D services to Amazon Leo's customers. The organization operates through three sub-functions: (i) Shaping Policy: leads public consultations, advocacy, and rulemakings at national, regional, and international levels to secure country entry, improve licensing frameworks, enable spectrum access, and prevent undesirable compliance requirements on Amazon Leo; (ii) Securing Authorizations: obtains the licenses required across broadband and D2D services and engages regulators to resolve licensing barriers and secure spectrum access and use rights; and (iii) Executing on Obligations: establishes Lawful Intercept (LI) and Law Enforcement Response (LER) programs by jurisdiction, fulfills the spectrum and network related obligations attached to held authorizations, and demonstrates compliance with service obligations. These obligations range from absolute (e.g., LI/LER) to defensible (e.g., certifications, reporting, fees, content blocking, regulator engagement), where failure carries fines, license revocations, service disruptions, and reputational damage.
The team partners with Business, Legal, Public Policy, and Public Relations to execute the strategy, and align with Design, Engineering, Operations, Security, and Business teams to keep the Plan of Record (POR) synchronized with regulatory requirements.

- Experience working with regulatory agencies such as the FCC, ITU, or equivalent national regulators and interpreting license conditions and translating regulatory obligations into engineering or operational requirements.

title: Director; Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) (Remote)
location: Remote - USA
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
MISUMI Americas serves customers through regional sourcing teams and a network of QCTs (warehouses) that hold inventory close to demand. As the business grows, we need one clear, trusted process that connects what sales expects to sell with what we source, build and stock. This role creates and owns that process.
The Director, SIOP is the practice lead for Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning. Each month, they bring together a top-down view (business plan, targets, market signals) and a bottom-up view (account and regional forecasts) over a rolling horizon of six months or more. They turn that consensus demand into requirements by region and into the inventory each QCT must hold. Where supply cannot meet demand, they make the gap visible, size the impact on customer service and revenue, and consolidate the proposed fixes into clear investment options for the executive team.
The Director, SIOP is a peer of the Directors, Portfolio Management and works with them as partners. Portfolio Management owns what we offer: assortment, pricing, launches, exits and supplier capability. SIOP owns how much, where and when: consensus demand, regional supply requirements, QCT inventory targets and the monthly planning process. Phase 1 covers standard and configurable products and QCT inventory; custom process lines are covered through demand and partner-capacity visibility.
This is a Director role with a player-coach start: the person runs the process hands-on at first, then builds a small, highly capable team of planners and analysts. Success is measured by forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns.
Own the monthly SIOP cycle: Design, run and keep improving the monthly process end to end: data refresh, demand review, supply review, reconciliation and the executive SIOP meeting. Set the calendar, the inputs each team owes and the decisions each step must produce.
Own the consensus demand number: Combine the business plan and targets with account and regional forecasts from Sales and the category overlay from each Portfolio Manager (launches, price changes, exits, competitive moves). Reconcile the views, explain the gaps and agree one demand plan over a rolling horizon of six months or more. Sales owns the account forecast; Portfolio Managers own the assumptions in their overlay; SIOP owns the process and the final number.
Translate demand into regional requirements: Map the consensus forecast to supply requirements by region, so regional sourcing teams know what volume and mix they must secure, and when.
Set inventory policy and QCT targets: Define safety stock, reorder logic and stocking depth by QCT and SKU class, to meet the service levels agreed in the executive SIOP review within the working-capital envelope set by Finance. Portfolio Managers decide which items are in the stocked set; SIOP decides how deep and where. Plan the run-down of items Portfolio Management decides to exit.
Run the input scorecard: Track whether Sales, Portfolio Management and Sourcing deliver complete, on-time and credible inputs each month, and publish the scorecard. The VP, Portfolio Management is the executive sponsor, chairs the monthly review and escalates late or weak Portfolio Management inputs. Late or weak Sales inputs escalate to the executive leadership team through the scorecard. The SVP, Operations & Supply Chain co-sponsors the supply-side inputs (Sourcing and QCTs) and escalates those.
Find and size supply and demand mismatches: Identify where demand will exceed supply or capacity, or where we hold inventory that demand does not support. Quantify revenue at risk and service impact. The relevant Portfolio Manager proposes the fix for their category or process; SIOP consolidates the proposals into the executive pre-read.
Lead the executive SIOP review: Prepare a concise monthly pre-read and run the executive meeting. Frame the decisions needed (investment, allocation, stocking, capacity), record what was decided and follow up on actions to closure.
Own the planning metrics: Define, measure and report forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns. Set targets with the executive team and drive improvement over time.
Build the tools and data foundation: Work with Finance, Business Systems and Data teams to establish the planning data model, forecast history and dashboards the process needs. Choose and implement planning tools as the practice scales.
Build the team: Hire, develop and lead a small, high-performing team of demand and supply planners or analysts as the practice grows.
All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
Required
Experience: 10+ years in demand planning, supply planning, S&OP / IBP or supply chain operations, with at least 3–5 years leading the S&OP or SIOP process for a multi-region business.
Built a process before: A track record of designing and launching a monthly S&OP / SIOP cycle (not only taking part in one), and making it stick across sales, operations and finance.
Strong analytical skills: Fluent in forecasting methods, inventory policy (safety stock, service levels, reorder points) and capacity planning. Advanced Excel / Google Sheets; comfortable with BI tools and large data sets.
Influence without authority: Proven ability to hold sales and operations leaders accountable for inputs and commitments they do not report to you for.
Works as a peer of category owners: Gets the commercial story from category owners and stays out of assortment and pricing decisions.
Executive communication: Can turn complex planning data into a short, clear story with options and trade-offs for senior leaders.
Business judgment: Can build an investment case that links inventory and capacity decisions to service levels, revenue and working capital.
Leadership: Experience hiring and developing planners or analysts, or a strong readiness to build a team from scratch.
Education: Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, engineering, business or a related field.
Preferred
Industry: Experience in industrial distribution, manufacturing, configurable components or a high-SKU, make-to-order and stock business.
Network inventory: Experience setting inventory policy across a network of warehouses or distribution centers.
Planning tools: Hands-on experience with planning platforms (for example, Kinaxis, o9, Anaplan, SAP IBP or similar) and ERP data.
Global and matrixed work: Experience in a multinational company, including work with a parent company or stakeholders across cultures and time zones.
Certification: APICS / ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) or similar is a plus; an MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
AI and automation: Interest in using AI and automation to improve forecasting and reduce manual planning work.
Primarily remote, computer-based work, including extended periods at a computer and on video calls. Occasional visits to QCT (warehouse) and supplier sites, which involve walking, standing and following site safety rules.
Ability to travel up to 20% annually, mainly within the Americas, for QCT and regional sourcing visits, team meetings and offsites, with occasional international travel to work with MISUMI Group planning teams.
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs
Salary Range:  $194,360 - $245,220 per year; based upon experience
We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates
We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

Global Operations Specialist
Help our customers improve their global supply chains
The Opportunity:
At Flexport, we know global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global trade easier for everyone. Flexport today connects more than 10,000 clients, both consignees and shippers, across 112 countries. Our role is to help businesses of all sizes find the global trade solutions that will empower their success.

As a new team member in our North American Operations group, you'll begin by immersing yourself in our company culture and mastering world-class operations. As Flexport continues to grow, there could be opportunities for future Flexporters to become founding team members in new markets, relocate internationally, and help us expand our presence around the world. If you're interested in a fast-paced career with the potential for international experience, this opportunity could offer you unmatched growth and adventure.

Be responsible for executing the movement of ocean and air freight shipments from booking at origin to final delivery at destination.
Maintain communications with Flexport transportation and warehousing partners to facilitate the progress of shipments in transit.
Work and communicate cross-functionally within Flexport
Be a part of the frontline groups ensuring the highest standard of Flexport quality: shipments move on time and exceptions are handled appropriately.
Use metrics to spot opportunities to improve and deliver great performance in your role.
Own the data quality of our client's information by validating booked shipments, tracking client shipment status, and validating shipment schedules.
Consistently follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure that your work satisfies internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) in line with productivity goals.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail in a high-energy, fast-paced environment.

A "compliance first" attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry.

title: IT Systems & Automation Lead - Bolingbrook
location: Chicago, IL || Bolingbrook, IL
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI-native, technically resourceful operator to rethink how IT works at Formic. You'll own the day-to-day technology experience for Formicans, from devices, applications, and employee support to infrastructure, security fundamentals, and external technology partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with significant autonomy: you'll solve immediate problems while building smarter, more reliable systems that prevent them from recurring.
If the Wi-Fi is down, someone's account isn't working, a conference room isn't connecting, a new hire needs a laptop, or a critical application goes offline, you're the person who makes sure it gets handled. You aren't expected to personally pull every cable, configure every system, or solve every specialized security issue. You are expected to own the outcome.
You don't need to know every system we use on Day 1. We'd rather hire someone with strong technical fundamentals, exceptional resourcefulness, and an ability to learn quickly. Over time, we expect you to become an expert in Formic's technology environment and help shape how our systems evolve as we grow.
You do need to be highly capable at using AI to extend what you can do. We want someone who is genuinely excited about technology and constantly asks: Why are we doing this manually? Can I automate it? Can I make this better?
AI and automation are central to this job, not side projects. We want someone who connects AI to real systems and workflows, builds practical automations, experiments responsibly, and measures whether their work makes Formic faster and more effective.
The goal is simple: technology becomes something the company rarely has to think about because it simply works.
In this role, you will:
Own Employee IT
Serve as the internal owner of day-to-day IT support, troubleshooting issues across Mac and Windows devices, applications, accounts, authentication, peripherals, and connectivity.
Own the technology experience throughout the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning and recovery, account configuration, permissions, and secure access removal.
Administer our device fleet, including MDM/RMM, patching, encryption, endpoint protection, software deployment, remote management, and remote lock/wipe capabilities.
Maintain an accurate hardware inventory and manage the full equipment lifecycle, including purchasing, configuration, deployment, repairs, replacements, shipping, and returns.
Administer systems such as Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, 1Password, Microsoft 365, Apple Business Manager, VPN, and other SaaS applications.
Manage identities, accounts, groups, permissions, licenses, MFA, SSO, and application access.
Maintain clear, accurate, and accessible documentation of our systems, configurations, processes, and administrative access.
Establish effective IT support processes for request intake, prioritization, escalation, resolution tracking, and employee communication.
Identify recurring issues, address root causes, and implement solutions that reduce support requests and improve the employee technology experience.
Own IT Infrastructure & Office Technology
Own the reliability and functionality of our internet, Wi-Fi, networking, conference rooms, displays, AV equipment, printers, shared devices, and other onsite technology.
Manage and troubleshoot network infrastructure, including routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points, VPNs, and connectivity issues.
Own the technology supporting physical security, including badge access systems and security cameras, partnering with internal teams and external specialists as needed.
Ensure conference rooms and shared technology are consistently reliable, functional, and ready for use.
Resolve onsite technology issues and coordinate with ISPs, network engineers, low-voltage contractors, security vendors, and other technical specialists when needed.
Drive technology installations, infrastructure upgrades, office expansions, and other IT-related projects.
Maintain organized and readily available IT equipment, spare devices, networking hardware, and accessories.
Proactively monitor infrastructure, anticipate potential issues, and implement improvements that minimize downtime and strengthen system reliability.
Automate Relentlessly
Use AI as a force multiplier in your own work, actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Identify repetitive, inefficient, or manual processes across IT operations and the broader Formic organization that can be eliminated, simplified, or automated.
Design, build, and maintain workflows using AI agents, APIs, scripts, integrations, and automation platforms.
Automate provisioning, onboarding, offboarding, technical support, inventory management, documentation, reporting, and other recurring IT processes wherever practical.
Build lightweight internal tools when developing a solution makes more sense than purchasing another piece of software.
Leverage AI to improve troubleshooting, system monitoring, knowledge management, and employee self-service.
Help Formic evaluate and adopt technologies that make our teams faster, smarter, and more effective.
Measure the effectiveness of automations and continuously improve our systems and processes with scalability, reliability, and security in mind.
Own IT Security Fundamentals & External Partners
Serve as Formic's internal owner of our managed IT and security provider relationships, maintaining accountability for systems, services, and outcomes.
Partner with external specialists on endpoint security, EDR/MDR, networking, vulnerability management, monitoring, and incident response.
Establish and maintain effective baseline security controls, including MFA, encryption, patching, endpoint protection, device management, and access controls.
Support SOC 2 and other compliance initiatives through accurate documentation, control implementation, system inventories, and evidence collection.
Maintain visibility into device compliance, vulnerabilities, access controls, and administrative privileges, ensuring identified risks are tracked through remediation.
Exercise sound technical judgment in determining what to resolve internally and when to engage external specialists.
Hold vendors accountable for responsiveness, service quality, timelines, costs, and outcomes.
Continuously evaluate the effectiveness of our external IT partnerships, identifying opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
Assess which IT capabilities should be developed internally versus supported by
Bonus Points if you have:
Worked in a startup or physical operating environment.
Administered Google Workspace, MDM/RMM, EDR, or identity systems.
Supported SOC 2 or other security compliance frameworks.
Worked effectively with external IT providers and held partners accountable for service quality and outcomes.
Worked with office networking, firewalls, VPNs, or physical-security systems.
Experience implementing or improving IT ticketing, asset management, monitoring, or employee self-service systems.
Built scripts, bots, internal tools, integrations, or AI agents because you got tired of doing something manually.
Created a home lab, side project, GitHub repo, Raspberry Pi graveyard, overly complicated Home Assistant setup, or other evidence that you genuinely enjoy messing with technology also counts.
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy

description:
In this role, you’ll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration. You will have an opportunity to drive cutting-edge TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) technology that powers Google's most demanding AI/ML applications. You’ll be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's TPU. You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide, and leverage your design and verification expertise to verify complex digital designs, with a specific focus on TPU architecture and its integration within AI/ML-driven systems.
Every custom Google Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) begins with its physical building blocks—foundry Process Design Kits (PDKs), standard cell libraries, high-speed memories, and specialized third-party Intellectual Property (IP). As an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) Computer-Aided Design (CAD) IP Engineer, you will sit at the intersection of external semiconductor ecosystems and Google's Artificial Intelligence (AI) hardware tapeouts. Rather than managing silicon collateral manually, you will engineer automated Python and Tcl validation pipelines that transform foundry and vendor deliveries into clean, unified, production-ready releases. Your automation and quality gates directly safeguard multi-billion-transistor TPU schedules, catching cross-view discrepancies before they reach physical implementation and signoff. Because you will partner with Physical Design, Static Timing Analysis (STA), CAD Methodology, and foundry partners, this role offers an end-to-end view of advanced-node chip execution—with direct mentorship and room to grow your ownership across Google's silicon infrastructure.
The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.
We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

title: Bid Desk Analyst
location: Troy - 701 S Ridge Ave
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
The Bid Desk Analyst supports the commercial and sales organization by coordinating and analyzing customer bid and quotation activities. This role serves as a central resource for managing requests for quotation (RFQs), gathering required information, analyzing pricing and cost data, and ensuring accurate, timely, and competitive bid submissions.
The Bid Desk Analyst works cross-functionally with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and other stakeholders to develop complete and commercially sound proposals. The position requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
· Coordinate and manage the bid and quotation process from initial request through submission.
· Review customer RFQs, bid requirements, specifications, and supporting documentation to identify requirements, deadlines, and potential risks.
· Gather and consolidate pricing, cost, lead time, product, freight, and other information required to prepare customer quotations.
· Analyze historical pricing, cost information, market data, and other relevant information to support pricing recommendations.
· Prepare accurate and competitive quotes in accordance with established pricing strategies, guidelines, and approval requirements.
· Partner with Sales and other internal stakeholders to clarify customer requirements and ensure bid responses are complete and accurate.
· Coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to obtain technical, operational, and financial inputs.
· Identify gaps, inconsistencies, or risks within bid requirements and escalate issues as appropriate.
· Maintain accurate bid documentation, pricing files, assumptions, and supporting information.
· Track open bids and quotation activity, including status, deadlines, submissions, and outcomes.
· Support analysis of bid win/loss results and identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
· Develop and maintain reports and dashboards related to bid activity, pricing, pipeline, and performance metrics.
· Assist with continuous improvement of bid desk processes, tools, templates, and workflows.
· Ensure pricing and quote information is handled confidentially and in accordance with company policies and controls.
· Provide timely follow-up and communication to ensure bids are completed and submitted within customer deadlines.
· Support strategic contract and bid opportunity assessment by analyzing customer buying patterns, renewal opportunities, competitive positioning, whitespace opportunities, historical performance, and profitability trends to inform bid strategy and commercial decision-making
· Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
· This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Education and Work Experience
· Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Marketing, or a related field or equivalent relevant work experience.
· 2+ years of relevant experience in quoting, pricing, sales operations, business analysis, customer service, supply chain, or a related field.
· Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
· Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
· Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.
· Strong written and verbal communication skills.
· Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
· Ability to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
Desired Education/Experience
· Experience working with RFQs, bids, proposals, or commercial pricing.
· Experience with ERP, CRM, CPQ, or other pricing/quotation systems.
· Experience analyzing pricing, margins, costs, and competitive information.
· Experience with Power BI or other data visualization/reporting tools.
Certificates and Licenses
No specific certificates or licenses are preferred or required.
Job —Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
· Bid, RFQ, and quotation processes
· Pricing, costing, margins, and commercial practices
· Customer and sales support processes
· Data analysis and reporting
· ERP/CRM/CPQ systems and Microsoft Excel
· Cross-functional business processes and internal controls
· Excellent MS Office (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word) capabilities required
COMPETENCIES
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies.
· Analytical Thinking: Uses data and sound judgment to evaluate information, identify trends, and support business decisions.
· Attention to Detail: Ensures accuracy and completeness of pricing, quotes, documentation, and customer requirements.
· Business Acumen: Understands the relationship between pricing, cost, margin, customer requirements, and business objectives.
· Collaboration: Builds effective working relationships across Sales, Operations, Finance, and other functions.
· Customer Focus: Understands customer needs and ensures bid responses are accurate, timely, and responsive.
· Organization & Prioritization: Effectively manages multiple bids, deadlines, and competing priorities.
· Communication: Clearly communicates requirements, assumptions, risks, and recommendations to internal stakeholders.
· Continuous Improvement: Identifies opportunities to improve the efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness of the bid process.
