description:
Job Description:
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for  Production Planner / Scheduler position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
Production Planner / Scheduler responsibilities are to review, and schedule work orders based on capacity and material availability to satisfy customer demands.  To execute Purchase Order releases for the demands associated with his or her assigned commodities. The Buyer / Planner is to utilize the ERP systems to plan, purchase, schedule and coordinate business requirements necessary for on-time production.  Function within policies and guidelines set forth by the Organization, establish production schedules and coordinate sources of supply for assigned material commodities with regard to total cost, quality, timely delivery and reliability. Buyer / Planner will have ownership of all the Inventory associated with the assigned commodities [item classes].
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Plan / Purchase and schedule production activities to achieve customer needs, marketing requirements, inventory and service level objectives while always ensuring a continuous production flow to manufacturing.
Based on business activity level, provide sales and business teams lead times for products.
Based on business activity level, manage the inventory to meet set goals for active, slow and obsolete inventory, while ensuring high levels of on-time delivery to customer requests.
Review schedules in production meeting to report the status of the supply chain. Advises appropriate individuals and departments of any delivery deviations that effect scheduled manufacturing orders.
Manage supply chain and production activity to ensure lead-times are maintained at a competitive level. Use macro level activity trending to recommend changes to resource levels.
Facilitate and encourage use of toolbox i.e. MRD and/or Kanban (visual inventory management from shop-floor), in-lining and USA in production. Demonstrate use of these techniques in various aspects of the job.
Release shop floor orders to production and strive to maximize on time delivery performance of assigned product line, use Auto Scheduling when possible.
Understand and communicate component specifications to suppliers, including the ability to read drawings.
Achieves metrics and objectives while working successfully in a team environment.
Regular attendance and the ability to follow all safety procedures.
Processes Engineering Change Notices (ECNs) in a timely manner and updates open Purchase Orders with suppliers to ensure correct revision levels are produced and delivered to Brooks.

Supports and implements company continuous improvement initiatives to ensure departmental goals and metrics are met.

Product Introduction Planning & Readiness Execution

Work closely with the Regional Leads who define the product launch roadmap into each country and lead the PMO GMA team to create detailed plans to support regional launches.
Ensure plans cover the necessary scope of activity required to achieve APL / launch readiness, with the necessary timelines and resources.
Assess cross-functional resource capacity and constraints needed to support regional launch roadmap. Escalate resource gaps and/or trade offs required to support successful execution

description:

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Team
The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.

MD or DO required.
Surgical or interventional specialty training preferred, but not required if the candidate demonstrates strong innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.

data integrity and scalability.

publications. Improve and implement SOPs and WIs for Statistical Analysis Plans (SAPs)

studies.

team members in best practices.

community.

interpersonal skills with both technical and non-technical constituents.

The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

The Cybersecurity Architect provides enterprise-level technical and architectural leadership to advance the organization’s cybersecurity strategy and long-term technology direction. description:
Job Description
The Manufacturing Manager is responsible for leading manufacturing operations within a large, complex food manufacturing facility with 1,000+ employees and USDA/FDA regulatory oversight. This role provides leadership across production operations with accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
The Manufacturing Manager will develop production leaders, drive Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS) principles, improve operational performance, and build a culture of accountability, employee engagement, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
As a key member of the Plant Leadership Team, this role partners closely with EHS, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, People & Performance, Supply Chain, Planning, and other functions. Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people objectives.
Ensure compliance with GMPs, food safety requirements, Kraft Heinz standards, and applicable USDA/FDA regulations.

Proven ability to deliver results across safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people performance.

title: National Account Manager C&U
location: United States of America
description:
Plan and execute the activities of promotion and sales in multiple areas in a given region. Generate, plan, and follow up daily and monthly sales targets and actuals to achieve the sales targets of the region. Support and approve initiation, expenditures, and implementation of investments to meet the company's business requirements. Work in close cooperation with sales force effectiveness and market research professionals to effectively utilize the sales representatives and look for training opportunities and assignments that would enable their personal and career development. Follow up and increase the performance of each sales representative in the region by making double visits and carrying out periodical coaching. This is a first level of sales management.
Job Purpose
​​As a National Account Manager, you will be responsible for a specified channel. This role is uniquely positioned for an ambitious leader who is craving full ownership and accountability for our products and customers within the assigned Accounts. This is not a traditional sales role. We are searching for a candidate who shows a high level of ownership for their business and is adept at selling solutions and has a proven ability to win new business. We are seeking a candidate who is eager to be a leader, influencer and activator with internal and external key stakeholders from the first day on the job. ​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Serve as a key liaison between Kraft Heinz, the Sales organization, and assigned customers and partners, building strong relationships that drive profitable growth within the Non-Commercial Foodservice segment.
Develop and lead channel-specific priorities across K-12, College & University (C&U), Business & Industry (B&I), and Healthcare to deliver quarterly and annual growth goals, increase market penetration, and grow market share.
Manage and develop relationships across GPO/CMC partners, including Foodbuy/Compass, Entegra/Sodexo, Aramark/Avendra, Premier, and Vizient, while identifying opportunities to establish new Non-Commercial partnerships.
Serve as a subject matter expert within the Non-Commercial segment, using market, customer, insights, and sales data to identify opportunities, analyze performance gaps, target potential customers, and develop data-driven growth strategies.
Develop, track, analyze, and evaluate customer and channel business plans based on Kraft Heinz priorities, customer strategies, and external market factors to drive total customer profitability.
Lead Joint Business Planning with strategic and small-to-mid-tier accounts, tailoring programs to customer strategies while aligning with Kraft Heinz business objectives.
Build and manage a profitable sales pipeline, driving conversion of opportunities and identifying incremental branded opportunities with new and existing customers.
Grow assigned customer business through achievement of revenue and profitability targets, share gains, new and core item distribution, and effective management of Customer P&L and EBITDA objectives.
Develop customer selling stories and recommendations using insights, analytics, and market data to support business opportunities and influence customer decisions.
Develop and track Non-Commercial KPIs and sales metrics, regularly communicating wins, performance gaps, pipeline progress, and areas of opportunity during key sales meetings and business reviews.
Prepare and present periodic customer business reviews, effectively communicating business performance, opportunities, recommendations, and forward-looking strategies.
Lead and support contract negotiations, deal creation, customer presentations, and other commercial discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
Guide trade-spend strategy by channel, evaluate program ROI, and recommend or negotiate adjustments to maximize the effectiveness and profitability of trade investments.
Partner cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Legal, Culinary, Marketing, R&D, and other key stakeholders to develop customer programs, new SKUs, sales collateral, and solutions that support execution of business plans.
Support S&OP and forecasting processes, including demand planning and waste-mitigation efforts.
Challenge internal and external teams to think creatively, develop new solutions, and capitalize on emerging business opportunities.
Demonstrate strong financial and analytical acumen, including the ability to build business cases, evaluate ROI, interpret sales performance, and influence P&L outcomes.
Operate with an entrepreneurial, action-oriented mindset, demonstrating ownership, sound decision-making, perseverance, and the ability to solve complex business problems.
Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication, presentation, influence, and negotiation skills across both internal and external stakeholders.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sales, or related field preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
​Prior sales experience required with a demonstration of major account management resulting in profitable volume, customer penetration, attainment of new business and growth.
​Experience in national accounts sales, restaurant, culinary, and/or distributor industry preferred. Experience within the Education (K-12, Colleges, University) channel preferred.
​Command of business acumen and strong business intuition demonstrated by discernment that not every sales opportunity is equal and a track record of securing profitable volume and walking away from less profitable deals.
​Strong analytical skills demonstrated by previous experience utilizing systems for tracking and recording sales, effective business planning and data-driven strategy for maintaining current and securing new customers.
​Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, demonstrated by effective presentation, influence, and advanced negotiation skills with both internal and external stakeholders.
​Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
​Must have a valid driver’s license and meet MVR requirements.
​Overnight Travel is required, and the amount varies by territory.​
Work Environment & Schedule
This position is considered a Remote based role that can be performed from a home office with expected travel. Additionally, this role requires working a salaried, exempt schedule to best execute against customer and internal expectations.

Digital Transformation Reinvention (DTR) is a strategic enterprise-wide transformation that brings together Digital Foundations, Value Creation, Digital Products, Data & AI, DT Talent, and Digital Upskilling to enable new ways of working and accelerate business outcomes. As Change Lead, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring leaders, managers, and associates are prepared, enabled, and supported to successfully adopt and sustain the changes required to deliver transformation results.
This is a highly influential, hands-on leadership role focused on enterprise organizational change rather than program management, communications delivery, or workstream ownership. The successful candidate will translate complex and often ambiguous transformation initiatives into a clear change architecture, targeted interventions, and measurable adoption outcomes. Working closely with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, you will drive readiness, sponsorship, behavior change, and adoption across a large-scale global transformation, ensuring benefits are realized and sustained over time.
What Are We Looking For?
Bachelor's degree in Business, Organizational Development, Human Resources, Psychology, Change Management, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Relevant change management certification preferred.
8+ years of progressive experience leading enterprise-wide digital, technology, operating model, workforce, or business transformation initiatives within complex global organizations.
Deep expertise in organizational change management, including readiness assessment, stakeholder engagement, adoption, behavior change, and sustainment.
Proven success developing and executing enterprise change strategies, sponsorship models, impact assessments, adoption frameworks, and intervention plans that drive measurable business outcomes.

Experience establishing adoption metrics, readiness measures, dashboards, and feedback mechanisms to monitor progress, evaluate effectiveness, and drive continuous improvement.
Proven ability to work effectively within global matrix organizations, coordinating enterprise-wide initiatives while enabling local market or segment activation.
Strong judgment and professionalism when handling sensitive, confidential, or incomplete information.
Experience supporting transformations involving digital products, data and AI, technology modernization, enterprise capability building, workforce upskilling, and/or federated global organizations preferred.
What Will Be Your Key Responsibilities?
Lead Enterprise Change Strategy & Transformation Adoption
Define and lead the enterprise change strategy and implementation roadmap for Digital Transformation Reinvention (DTR).
Develop and maintain an integrated change architecture that links transformation objectives to impacted audiences, required behavior shifts, readiness risks, interventions, and adoption measures.
Translate transformation priorities into clear people, capability, leadership, and behavior requirements.
Establish change management standards, governance, methodologies, and best practices across transformation workstreams.
Integrate change, readiness, and adoption milestones into the overall transformation roadmap.
Assess Organizational Impact & Drive Readiness
Lead enterprise-wide assessments across people, processes, technology, governance, roles, skills, and ways of working.
Maintain a comprehensive view of stakeholder impacts, organizational readiness, and adoption risks across the transformation portfolio.
Identify resistance points, adoption barriers, and critical dependencies, implementing mitigation plans to address risks proactively.
Ensure impact assessments and readiness plans evolve as transformation priorities, scope, or design decisions change.
Enable Leaders, Managers & Sponsors to Drive Change
Define and activate a sponsorship model that promotes visible leadership ownership of transformation outcomes.
Coach and equip senior leaders and managers to confidently lead teams through ambiguity, change, and transition.
Design and implement interventions that move key stakeholder groups from awareness and understanding to adoption, advocacy, and sustained behavior change.
Partner with leaders to reinforce the actions and behaviors necessary for successful transformation adoption.
Partner Across Workstreams & Segments
Collaborate with transformation workstream leaders to embed change management into solution design and delivery.
Coordinate with segment and market counterparts to validate impacts, assess readiness, and support local activation efforts.
Maintain a unified enterprise approach to stakeholder engagement, communication, and leadership action.
Surface cross-functional and cross-segment adoption risks, dependencies, and challenges for leadership decision-making and escalation.
Measure Adoption & Sustain Transformation Outcomes
Define and track leading and lagging indicators that measure readiness, adoption, behavior change, and business value realization.
Establish readiness baselines and maintain enterprise adoption dashboards that provide actionable insights.
Monitor adoption progress, evaluate intervention effectiveness, and recommend course corrections when needed.
Create feedback loops that translate stakeholder insights into meaningful improvements and sustainable business outcomes.
Partner with Change Communications & Key Stakeholders

Provide readiness, stakeholder, and adoption insights that inform communication priorities, audience engagement, and sequencing.

About Mars Petcare
Mars Petcare is proud to actively recruit, develop, and promote transitioning military service members and veterans. Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity—the chance to leverage the leadership, operational discipline, and mission focus gained during your military career to direct world-class supply chains that produce beloved global pet care brands like Greenies.

We are seeking an experienced Logistics Lead for our overnight operations (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) in North Kansas City, MO. In this specialized individual contributor and frontline leadership role, you will oversee day-to-day distribution and transportation activities, coordinate with freight carriers and third-party logistics (3PL) partners, manage transactional inventory data systems, and ensure seamless throughput across our evening operating window.
This position is ideally suited for transitioning military non-commissioned officers (NCOs), petty officers, warrant officers, or logistics officers with proven experience leading personnel, managing assets under tight timelines, and directing transportation movements.
What Are We Looking For? (Requirements)
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent level of verified military/professional experience.
Relevant Experience: 3 to 6 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, distribution, or transportation operations, demonstrating the judgment to handle unexpected operational hurdles and advise cross-functional teammates.
Leadership & Supervision: Proven background supervising and directing personnel, equipment, and resources to achieve mission-critical goals under tight deadlines.
Coordination Experience: Demonstrated track record (at least 4 to 6 months) of planning, organizing, and orchestrating the daily work assignments of team members.
Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to brief operational status, communicate clearly with external carriers, and maintain shift accountability.
Partnership & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships and collaborate across production, warehousing, and carrier networks to achieve shared performance targets.
Shift Availability: Dedicated availability to work the overnight schedule (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM).
Key Responsibilities
Transportation & Distribution Operations:
Provide operational oversight for overnight distribution workflows, serving as the first-line leader for transactional operations in shipping, receiving, and staging.
Coordinate activities of third-party carriers, subcontractors, and freight vendors, serving as their primary operational point of contact during the night shift under an established contract management framework.
Ensure all distribution operations comply with safety standards, quality control protocols, and Mars operating procedures.
Systems & Data Management:
Utilize enterprise warehouse and transportation data management systems (WMS/TMS) to access real-time shipping data, track order fulfillment, reconcile manifests, and manage bill of lading (BOL) documentation.
Monitor performance indicators (KPIs) to spot movement bottlenecks and execute proactive recovery plans.
Stakeholder & Supplier Coordination:
Maintain strong relationships with external logistics providers and internal plant teams, resolving operational escalations and ensuring on-time delivery schedules.
Support client- and vendor-facing communication, handling inquiries with clarity and professionalism.
Team Leadership & Development:
Supervise, coach, and mentor night shift operational associates, fostering a high-accountability safety and continuous improvement culture.
Pursue personal professional development through formal and informal Mars learning initiatives while developing training opportunities for team members.
Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) Crosswalk
Your military experience translating complex mission requirements, managing tight schedules, coordinating cargo movements, and leading teams provides directly transferable skills for this role. Candidates with backgrounds in the following service specialties are strongly encouraged to apply:
U.S. Army
MOS 88N (Transportation Management Coordinator): Direct match for freight scheduling, cargo booking, carrier coordination, commercial transport documentation, and movement control system management [source: 1, 6].
MOS 92A (Automated Logistical Specialist - NCO): Excellent alignment with warehouse data management systems, staging, transaction auditing, and supervising inventory operations.
MOS 88M (Motor Transport Operator - Squad Leader / Truck Master): Proven capability managing distribution lines, coordinating vehicle/asset movements, enforcing safety protocols, and leading personnel under shift deadlines.
MOS 92Y (Unit Supply Specialist - NCO / Supply Sergeant): Deep experience with property accountability, vendor coordination, inventory systems, and transactional operations.
Branch 88A / 90A (Transportation / Logistics Officer): Directly translates to leading operational distribution, carrier execution, contract alignment, and cross-functional team supervision.
U.S. Navy
Rating LS / LSS (Logistics Specialist / Logistics Specialist Submarine - Petty Officer): Strong match for inventory data system operations, shipping/receiving supervision, carrier liaison, receipt documentation, and supply chain accountability.
Rating CS / CSC (Culinary Specialist - Logistics & Provisioning Leads): Extensive experience in perishable goods distribution, inventory tracking systems, vendor receiving, and quality assurance.
Designator 3100 (Supply Corps Officer): Highly relevant experience directing end-to-end supply chains, freight handling, contractor oversight, and operational logistics leadership.
U.S. Air Force
AFSC 2T0X1 (Traffic Management Operations - TMO): Direct match for booking freight carriers, processing cargo documentation, monitoring contractor compliance, and managing inbound/outbound transit [source: 9, 29].
AFSC 2G0X1 (Logistics Plans): Direct alignment with distribution pipeline tracking, timeline execution, carrier coordination, and deployment/distribution logistics.
AFSC 2S0X1 (Materiel Management - Craftsman / Supervisor): Expert background in automated logistics systems, inventory accuracy, and supervising warehouse operational teams.
AFSC 21R (Logistics Readiness Officer): Demonstrated leadership directing intermodal transit, warehousing operations, contractor performance, and shift teams.
U.S. Marine Corps
MOS 3112 / 3152 (Distribution Management Specialist / Distribution Specialist): Directly translates to managing commercial freight movements, carrier dispatch, documentation, and cargo distribution networks [source: 11, 21].
MOS 0431 / 0441 (Logistics / Embarkation Specialist): Proven ability in multi-modal movement planning, load coordination, staging, and cargo manifest reconciliation [source: 3, 18].
MOS 3043 (Supply Chain and Materiel Management Specialist): High-level capability in inventory management systems, supplier coordination, and supervising material handlers.
MOS 0402 (Logistics Officer): Broad expertise managing operational supply distribution, transport planning, third-party logistics support, and leadership.

description:
Job Description:
Job: Material Handler
Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)
Location: North Kansas City, MO
Shift: Night Shift (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) on a 2-2-3 Rotating Schedule (Alternating weekends off)
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.

Job Description:
The SRM Pricing & Promotions Manager supports the Strategic Demand team and the US and Canadian Sales teams in driving Strategic Revenue Management (SRM) initiatives towards profitable growth for Mars Food North America and for our customers. This associate leads the creation of market portfolio pricing and promotion strategy, development of annual pricing and promotion plans, and overall management of market pricing and promotion practices.
The SRM Pricing & Promotion Manager is a member of the broader North America Strategic Demand Leadership team. Reporting to the Strategic Revenue Management Lead, this associate will work closely with sales teams and marketing/finance partners to optimize Mars Food revenue and profitability. The primary scope of SRM is to drive increased trade investment productivity, net price realization and improved mix. This includes collaborating across the organization to optimize pack-price architecture, program of pay for performance conditions, and overall Trade ROI.
What are we looking for?
Bachelor degree in business, finance, economics, math or sciences. Graduate level preferred.
3-5+ years of experience in a blue chip FMCG/consumer products company and an analytical and commercial background.
undefined
Experience with revenue management, P&L management, or financial accounts.
Experience working with retail POS data – Nielsen, IRI, etc.
Direct experience evaluating and optimizing retail promotions for volume lift and financial ROI.
Understanding of pricing strategy and the end-to-end steps required to deploy cost price changes within a market.
Strong track record of translating strategies into action and delivering results.
Strong leadership and influencing capability.

Azure Memory and Storage Center of Excellence (AMS CoE) is part of the SCHIE organization focusing on memory and storage devices going into the cloud hardware servers. AMS provides memory and storage solutions to Azure and drives memory and storage suppliers to deliver high quality products that meet our requirements. AMS CoE also leads Azure Fault Prediction and Detection (AFPD), the platform that predicts, detects and repairs hardware failures across the Azure fleet.
We are looking for a Cloud Principal Hardware Engineer to scale AFPD across hardware components in the Azure fleet and to lead hands-on hardware resiliency for the platform.
The opportunity:
Every hour a server sits unhealthy is an hour of lost customer capacity. AFPD turns hardware, firmware and OS telemetry into early detection and prediction of failures, moves customer workloads off failing nodes, and sends a targeted repair for the part that failed. Repair outcomes and supplier failure analysis then improve the next rule or model.
You will be working on incorporating into the platform components such as storage, memory, power supply, CPU, GPU, NIC, HBA/FPGA, cables and the rest of the server, and you will be the subject matter expert the team relies on when a failure needs to be prevented. Across millions of nodes, each improvement means fewer VM interruptions for customers and faster return of online capacity.
Why this role:
Your impact shows up in fleet availability and customer uptime, quarter over quarter. You will set the hardware direction for a platform that influences production infrastructure at a scale, and you will work directly with Azure engineering, component teams and leading hardware suppliers.
#SCHIE #azurehwjobs

Lead failure analysis across server components: characterize failure modes from fleet telemetry and logs and confirm root cause with repair results and supplier failure analysis.
Define the signals, thresholds, targeted diagnostics and repair recipes, and work with component teams for the root cause analysis.
Improve isolation accuracy so each repair address the source of failures: improve efficacy of the detection and repair services.
Partner with software engineers and data scientists on detection rules and prediction models; set precision targets and validation gates before a rule or model takes action on production nodes.
Use AI agents and machine learning to automate failure analysis, live-site triage and supplier RCA follow-up, and to shorten the time from a new failure signature to a detection rule.
Lead root cause and corrective actions with server components, including firmware fixes, and feed the learnings back into the platform.
Lead as the senior hardware escalation point for live-site incidents, from triage through root cause to fleet-wide mitigation.
Make new server generations and AI/GPU platforms platform-ready before they reach production, with detection, isolation and repair coverage at launch.
Track and improve metrics & mentor engineers across the team.

This role will drive the transition from fragmented systems and manual processes toward a connected, scalable digital execution platform that improves operational efficiency, data visibility, collaboration, and delivery predictability. The Digital Transformation Program Manager will own the AMERS EPC digital transformation roadmap, leading the evaluation, integration, implementation, and adoption of enterprise platforms, automation capabilities, and AI-enabled solutions. Working across Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Controls, Commissioning, and other delivery functions, this individual will translate complex business requirements into integrated technical solutions that support end-to-end project execution. The candidate will combine technical program management expertise, enterprise platform knowledge, construction industry understanding, and strategic leadership to establish a sustainable digital ecosystem that enables AMERS EPC to scale effectively.

Establish digital transformation priorities that support consistent execution across the Americas.

Lead the evaluation and implementation of digital solutions that improve project visibility, document management, workflow coordination, and construction execution.
Identify opportunities to consolidate redundant tools and reduce reliance on manual data collection and reporting.

Evaluate emerging technologies, including Microsoft Power Platform, Copilot, and AI-driven analytics, for practical application within EPC operations.
Translate operational challenges into technical requirements, solution concepts, and measurable business outcomes.
Lead pilots and experiments to validate proposed technologies, assess business value, and inform broader deployment decisions.
Establish scalable approaches for transitioning successful pilots into sustainable enterprise capabilities.

Define program objectives, technical requirements, implementation milestones, dependencies, risks, and success criteria.

Define requirements for data quality, governance, accessibility, consistency, and system interoperability.
Support the development of integrated dashboards, portfolio reporting capabilities, and predictive analytics.
Enable improved visibility into project schedules, milestones, risks, construction progress, and delivery performance.

description:
Overview
Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) is the organization that builds, operates, and continuously evolves the infrastructure behind the Microsoft Cloud, powering services used by more than 95% of Fortune 500 companies. CO+I is responsible for the full datacenter lifecycle from global planning and site acquisition through design, construction, deployment, operations, and eventual decommissioning, spanning 400+ datacenters across more than 70 Azure regions, connected by over 600,000 kilometers of fiber. As the engine that enables Microsoft’s cloud-first mission, CO+I delivers reliable, trusted, secure, and sustainable cloud and AI infrastructure, ensuring capacity is available on time, every time, to meet customer growth and support Microsoft’s broader mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more.
The Systems Engineering, Test, and Integration (SETI) team in the CO+I Office of the CTO evaluates and matures new datacenter technologies before they're deployed at scale. As a Mechanical Engineer, you'll work on the mechanical systems for first-of-a-kind cooling and test infrastructure, from analysis and design through construction, commissioning, and field validation. You'll connect thermal-fluid fundamentals, hydraulic behavior, controls, and field observations to deliver working systems.
Responsibilities
Evaluate, develop, and integrate next-generation mechanical infrastructure technologies, including liquid and air cooling systems, for Microsoft's datacenter portfolio.
Define system requirements, technical specifications, mechanical architectures, interfaces, and verification strategies for emerging infrastructure solutions.
Design and analyze hydronic and thermal-fluid systems, such as technology water loops, CDUs, heat exchangers, pumps, and piping. Use hydraulic network, pressure-drop, and CFD modeling, and validate model results against measured system data.
Develop design documentation, engineering specifications, CAD models, drawings, and technical recommendations that support technology maturation and deployment.
Translate design intent into field-executable work. This includes reviewing piping modifications, spool drawings, and contractor scopes, and resolving constructability and supplier–installer interface issues.
Create and execute test, validation, and verification plans, including startup, commissioning, hydraulic balancing, and controls validation of installed systems.
Lead root-cause investigations of mechanical system issues, such as low flow, air entrainment, filtration, fluid contamination, and piping failures, using modeling, test data, and field evidence.
Perform technical due diligence on new technologies , supplier solutions, and industry developments to inform engineering and deployment decisions.
Evaluate design alternatives and make recommendations based on performance, risk, cost, schedule, reliability, manufacturability, and operational impact.
Collaborate with controls, electrical, construction, operations, A&E partners, contractors, and suppliers to develop new mechanical infrastructure solutions.
Support prototype development, lab and field testing, and supplier manufacturing readiness. Capture lessons learned from field work and commissioning as reusable requirements, standards input, and O&M guidance.

Professional Engineer (PE) license.
Experience with mechanical design and analysis tools (for example, CAD, FEA, CFD, or hydraulic network modeling) and with validating model results against test or field data.
Experience with datacenter or industrial hydronic and thermal-fluid systems, such as chilled-water plants, CRAHs, CDUs, liquid-cooled racks, pumps, and heat rejection.
Experience with construction, commissioning, or field engineering of mechanical systems, including pressure testing, flushing and passivation, and hydraulic balancing.

Every enterprise and government customer that builds on Microsoft's AI first asks the same question: can we prove it's secure and compliant? The Fundamentals Technical Program Management (TPM) team in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Infrastructure keeps Microsoft Foundry secure, compliant, reliable and available in every region where customers need it. You'll join a team that owns the programs every Foundry service depends on: security and compliance, privacy, reliability, business continuity and new-region readiness. You'll work in an AI-first way, using AI and AI agents to move faster and scale your impact. You'll partner with AI Infrastructure security and compliance leaders, engineering teams and Foundry product teams to earn and keep the trust of the most regulated customers in the world.   As a Principal Technical Program Manager for Standards, Audit Readiness and Operations, you'll independently own a large, ambiguous area: keeping AI Infrastructure's certifications current and audit-ready. These certifications include System and Organization Controls (SOC), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27001, the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), and ISO/IEC 42001, the standard for AI management systems. You'll set direction for the program and own delivery across several engineering teams. You'll turn regulatory requirements, as the security compliance team interprets them, into clear, actionable work, and drive readiness, risk closure and operating discipline so AI Infrastructure can respond to any audit request within one week. You'll use them to map new requirements to existing controls, draft audit responses, keep program status and risk reporting current, and spot bottlenecks before they slip a milestone. You'll design and develop agents that collect evidence, monitor controls and flag compliance gaps automatically. This keeps the organization ready for audits continuously instead of preparing for each one, and engineering spends less time on repetitive work. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.
This position is designed for a high-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign-ready approach.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment,  and trust-building priorities.
Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high-stakes community conversations.
Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.
Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.
Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.
Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.

Regional Leadership and Community Strategy
Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public  Community-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders.
Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high-impact venues.

Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.

Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit.
Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency, and continuous improvement.

Leverage clear escalation paths for operational, reputational, policy, permitting, media, and community issues, ensuring news travels fast and decision-makers receive concise, action-oriented guidance.

Overview
At Microsoft, we’re building a modern, AI-forward marketing organization that learns faster, activates smarter, and drives measurable impact. Our approach blends human creativity with AI-powered insights to fuel bold, culturally inspired creative strategies at scale. We prioritize outcomes over outputs, embrace rapid learning loops, and operate in agile flight formations that unite disciplines across Commercial Brand, Creative, and Customer Marketing.
This role is focused on the intersection of creators, content, and production.
For the last decade, brands treated social media as another channel to fill with content. Today, AI is reshaping how people discover information, create, learn, and connect. As content becomes easier to generate, the people behind it matter more than ever. Audiences don’t follow brands the way they follow people. They follow creators: individuals with a point of view, a voice, and a relationship with their community that no ad buy can replicate. Creators have become the new media companies, writing, shooting, editing, and distributing with a speed and authenticity traditional production struggles to match.
That shift changes what great brand content looks like, and how it gets made. Sometimes the best thing a brand can do is hand a creator a great brief and get out of the way. Other times, the work calls for a brand-quality shoot built around a creator, crafted to look a specific way, then published through their channels to their audience. Most of the time, it’s somewhere in between. Either way, someone has to make it run.
In this role, you will join Creator & Fandom, the team behind Microsoft’s creator and influencer programs, our in-house creator studio, and community programs. As Senior Creator Content Producer, you’ll be the production owner for creator work across campaigns, events, and community activations.
This isn’t a role where you’ll spend months taking notes from the sidelines. You’ll quickly take ownership of real productions that reach global audiences, work alongside creators and talent every week, and help shape how one of the world’s most iconic technology companies makes content with the people audiences actually trust.
At Microsoft, our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. With a growth‑mindset culture, we innovate responsibly and measure success by shared progress, people, teams, and customers. Join us to do meaningful work that changes the world and helps shape what’s next for everyone.

As a  Critical Environment Technician  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, recognizing safe versus unsafe work environment, having a hands-on understanding of how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.

As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members.  Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration.  - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

Translate technical information from technicians into simple, understandable language for owners. Proactively communicate updates on vehicle status, managing timelines and ensuring a transparent process. Coordinate with the Parts and Production teams to ensure all aspects of the service visit are aligned. Prepare and explain estimates and invoices with clarity and accuracy. Ensure every owner leaves feeling cared for, confident in the work performed, and more connected to the Rivian brand. Proven ability to manage senior stakeholders, including executives and external partners, and to negotiate and push back when needed. Strong written and verbal communication, including clear executive-level status, decision, and risk communication. Assemble VISTA Switch, both on the assembly line and directly on the shop floor.

title: Staff Hardware Test & Validation Lead (On-site)
location: Glen Cove, NY
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots, shipping at scale to customers ranging from small manufacturers to some of the largest companies in the country. We're hiring a technical lead to build and run a central hardware testing function to support product development across the company. You'll set and maintain a high bar for product quality, plan and resource test work, build and run setups from quick bench rigs to long-running validation at scale, and help the team troubleshoot and root-cause failures. The work covers robotic and electromechanical systems of all kinds. Hands-on IC technical lead role, working closely with the mechanical, electrical, and software engineering teams.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Test Process and Quality Standards. Guide and build a test and validation team, working closely with the hardware team. Standardize how hardware product validation is planned and run, and work with the hardware team to set quality standards. Help turn requirements and specs into test plans.

Planning and Scheduling. Plan and schedule test work and assign lab space, equipment, and people to it. Work closely with hardware and software teams on priorities and timing.

Testbeds, Fixtures, and Ad-Hoc Testing. Help review, design and build complex testbeds and fixtures, including mechanical design, instrumentation, and data acquisition. Run one-off tests from a spec or setup the hardware team provides, and scale them up when needed.

Product Validation and Long-Running Tests. Stand up and run product validation testing across many units, from component qualification to system-level performance tests. Define stop conditions, data products, and post-run inspection, and keep long tests running.

Documentation and Analysis. Strong documentation is a core skill for this role. Write test reports and analysis, procedures, and initial failure analysis. Keep documentation accurate and up to date.

Troubleshooting and Root Cause. Help mechanical and electrical engineers analyze complex failures and perform maintenance to keep hardware running. Engage with engineering teams to respond to and resolve failures.


TOOLS

Sensors and sensing (encoders, IMUs, accelerometers, image processing), data loggers & data collection interfaces, SolidWorks & PDM, oscilloscopes, thermal instrumentation, programming for data processing and analysis, Claude Code (or similar AI tools), typical business and productivity tools (Notion, Asana, Google Docs).


WHAT WE NEED


REQUIRED

 - BS in ME, EE, or similar (or equivalent experience)

 - 5+ years in hardware testing or validation, ideally in robotics, automotive, aerospace, medical, or a similar regulated or safety-critical domain

 - Experience taking complex validation plans from system requirements through test design, execution, and reporting

 - Experience leading and organizing test work, including planning, prioritizing, and assigning lab resources and people

 - Experience with root-cause investigations across ME / EE / FW boundaries

 - Comfortable writing test plans with clear pass/fail criteria and choosing sample sizes based on confidence needs

 - Hands-on with electrical instrumentation (scopes, probes, etc.) and reading schematics

 - Mechanical fundamentals including tolerance stacks, motor analysis, power transmission, bearings, fits, and structural design

 - Strong written documentation habits and experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Collaborative or industrial robots, or 6-DOF motion systems

 - Functional safety standards: ISO 13849, ISO 10218, IEC 61508, or ISO 26262

 - Mechanical / electrical design of fixtures and tooling

 - DFMEA / PFMEA or formal reliability practices

 - Failure analysis and root-cause analysis


WHERE THE ROLE GROWS

Over time, the role can expand to include:

 - Cross-Platform Test Strategy: own test strategy across platforms and set common test methods for every program

 - Lab Capability and Infrastructure: expand testing range and scope, plus test automation, fleet monitoring, and supporting infrastructure

 - Reliability Program: track MTBF / B-life and feed corrective actions back to design

 - Phase Gates and Design Reviews: represent testing at EVT/DVT/PVT gates and in DFMEA/PFMEA reviews

 - Technical Mentorship: mentor test engineers and technicians as the group grows

Compensation and Benefits:

The base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $200,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.
